entities.summary: Henry I of Nassau, German: Heinrich I. von Nassau, was the first person to name himself count of Nassau. Born in the 11th century, his exact birthdate is unknown. He is believed to have ruled the County of Nassau from 1056 until his death in 1167. Henry I's significance lies in his establishment of the County of Nassau as a major power in the Holy Roman Empire. He successfully negotiated the Treaty of Strasbourg with the Holy Roman Emperor, Frederick I, in 1135, securing recognition of his county's independence. This treaty marked a significant milestone in the development of the Holy Roman Empire's structure and paved the way for future conflicts. Henry I's legacy continued through his descendants, who would go on to shape the course of European history. He is remembered as a shrewd politician and a skilled diplomat, able to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries within the Holy Roman Empire. His contributions to the region's history are a testament to his enduring influence.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Henry I of Nassau's establishment of the County of Nassau as a major power in the Holy Roman Empire had significant consequences for the region. His successful negotiations with Emperor Frederick I led to the recognition of the county's independence, paving the way for future conflicts. The county's economic prosperity during this period helped to secure its position within the Holy Roman Empire, making it a significant player in regional politics.
